newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - AUGUST 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - AUGUST 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Government would battle hard to achieve its budget deficit target this year, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said on Tuesday, but it planned to address the crippling public service wage bill by negotiating a mechanism to reduce staff numbers.
- Callback operators will be banned in South Africa from September 1 in terms of a surprise first ruling by the newly formed South African Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (Satra).
- Police were investigating a claim that one of South Africa's provincial premiers has plotted an assassination, Justice Minister Dullah Omar said in Parliament on Tuesday.

- The planned takeover of Sentrachem by US-based Dow Chemicals Co for more than two billion rand is in the balance after the Sentrachem board decided on Monday to recommend that shareholders reject the offer of 10.50 rand a share.
- Tour operators and curio vendors will have to tread carefully when marketing Robben Island as a tourist attraction following a move by government to "patent" the name.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Sentrachem's share price surged 55 cents, or five percent, on Tuesday to close at 10.80 rand after its board rejected the 10.50 rand a share offer by the local subsidiary of U.S. group Dow Chemicals.
- De Beers, the diamond group, on Tuesday posted disappointing results in the half-year to June 30, with attributable earnings up five percent in dollar terms.

- International call-back operators were on Tuesday given tow weeks to shut down or face fines of up to 500,000 rand, two years in prison, or both by the South African Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (Satra).

- Mining house JCI's Beira iron project in Mozambique would be one of the most competitive projects of its kind in the world, and would be central to economic development in the country, Mzi Khumalo, the company's executive chairman said on Tuesday.

- The Namibian government was unlikely to grant South African Breweries and its Namibian partners permission to establish a 100 million rand brewery at Oshakati, Hidipo Hanutenya, the trade and industry minister, said on Tuesday.
SAKE BEELD
- The equity market is waiting for America's Dow Chemicals to raise its offer for Sentrachem after directors at Sentrachem rejected its offer yesterday.
- The South African economy got further evidence of a sharp downward trend in inflation on Tuesday, raising fresh expectations of an interest rate cut.
- The government has no immediate plans to replace Piet Liebenberg, who recently resigned as head of the South African Revenue Services.
- Telephone call-back operators have been banned from September 1 and face a fine of 500,000 rand or two years imprisonment if they continue to operate.
THE STAR

- Chris Hani was killed in order to plunge South Africa into chaos and prepare the ground for a right-wing coup, one of his murderers, Clive Derby-Lewis, told the Truth and Reconciliation Commission's amnesty committee on Tuesday.
- A baby female vervet monkey is recovering at the Johannesburg SPCA after it was rescued by police during a raid on a house in Cleveland, eastern Johannesburg, on Tuesday.
- The Greater Johannesburg Council has been blacklisted by one of South Africa's major credit-rating companies.
- If South Africa's sports bokkies are right, Bafana Bafana are already on their way France.
